title: Baize Event Log Entry
description: Schema for a single line in a Baize JSONL event log. Each line is an independent JSON object. Events are hash-chained: each entry includes the BLAKE3 hash of the previous entry, forming a tamper-evident Merkle chain for tournament integrity and mechanical diffing between Rust and Python implementations.

game_id.description: Unique identifier for the game session this event belongs to.

sequence.description: Zero-based monotonically increasing sequence number within this game's event log.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the event was emitted. Optional for deterministic replay; required for tournament logs.

player.description: The player who triggered or is affected by this event. Empty string for system events (game_over with no specific actor).

state_hash.description: BLAKE3 hash of the game state after this event has been applied.

prev_hash.description: BLAKE3 hash of the previous event (event_hash of sequence N-1). The first event uses the genesis hash: 64 zero characters.

event_hash.description: BLAKE3 hash of this event's canonical form, computed over the JSON serialization of {game_id, sequence, event_type, player, state_hash, prev_hash, payload} with keys sorted, compact separators (',', ':'), and UTF-8 encoding.

event_type.description: High-level event categories. move_applied: a player action was validated and applied. state_transition: engine-generated state change (turn advance, phase change, chain reaction). game_over: the game has ended. random_value: a random value was generated or revealed. visibility_check: a visibility query or hidden-state reveal occurred.

payload.description: Event-specific payload. Fields vary by event_type. All fields are optional to allow forward compatibility.

action.description: The specific action that was applied (for move_applied events).

component_id.description: Identifier of the component acted upon.

from.description: Source position as a coordinate string (e.g. '1,0').

to.description: Destination position as a coordinate string (e.g. '1,2').

captured.description: Identifier of a captured or removed component.

detail.description: Free-form detail string for additional context.

transition.description: The specific state transition (for state_transition events).

next_player.description: The player whose turn it is after a turn_advance transition.

outcome.description: How the game ended (for game_over events).

winner.description: The winning player (for game_over events with outcome 'win').

condition.description: Name of the end condition that triggered (e.g. 'three_in_a_row', 'checkmate').

random_type.description: Kind of randomness (e.g. 'roll', 'draw', 'shuffle') for random_value events.

random_result.description: The random value produced. Type varies: integer for dice, string for card draws, array for shuffles.

zone.description: Zone name relevant to this event.

revealed_to.description: Players who can see the revealed information.

final_scores.description: Final scores per player (for game_over events).

action_type.description: Specific player actions. These correspond to the action types in the Rust EventType enum and Python EventTypeLiteral (excluding engine-generated events turn_advance and game_end, which map to state_transition and game_over respectively).

transition_type.description: Engine-generated state transitions that are not direct player actions.
